options.metric: Annual number of pedestrians killed, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed across crashes.
options.denominator: None; this is an absolute annual count, not a rate or share.
options.reason: A line chart makes the sequence of annual pedestrian fatality counts and year-to-year changes easy to follow.
options.interpretation: The line chart answers the annual-count question by summing number_of_pedestrians_killed across police-reported NYC crash records and grouping by calendar crash year from 2013 through 2025; it shows a high of 176 in 2013, a low of 101 in 2020, and a fluctuating 107–135 per year from 2021 through 2025, ending at 119. This is a defensible framing because a line chart emphasizes the sequence of absolute year-to-year counts, with no denominator or exposure adjustment. It leaves unanswered rates relative to travel or population exposure and which crash characteristics explain these totals. The check found 0 missing pedestrian-death counts among the 2,132,218 in-scope crash rows, no missing crash dates in scope, and observed dates spanning January 1–December 31 in every requested year; all in-scope rows are retained, while records outside the requested years are excluded by the date filter.
